title: Getting started with R-itable
text: R-itable estimates narrow-sense heritability (h²) quantitative traits family cohort studies using profile-likelihood variance-components approach, without requiring SOLAR Eclipse proprietary software. three main steps : Build additive genetic relationship matrix (GRM) pedigree. Estimate heritability one trait herit_vc(). Scale many traits herit_batch(), visualise plot_forest(). twin cohorts specifically – monozygotic relatedness, household/shared- environment effects, bivariate genetic/environmental correlations two traits – see vignette("twin-cohorts") instead/addition.

title: Getting started with R-itable
text: build_grm() takes pedigree data frame returns additive genetic relationship matrix (GRM, also written ). GRM encodes much genetic material two individuals share due common ancestry, cornerstone variance-components model. pedigree needs four columns: Importantly, pedigree contain everyone — study subjects want analyse parents/grandparents (founders), even founders phenotype data. Including founders lets kinship2 trace shared ancestry correctly. example , IDs 1–4 two unrelated founder couples. IDs 5–6 offspring couple 1×2, IDs 7–8 offspring couple 3×4. study subjects IDs 5–8. Reading matrix: Diagonal = 1 non-inbred individuals (person shares 100% genome ). 5 & 6 share 0.5 — full siblings (parents 1×2), share average half segregating alleles. 7 & 8 share 0.5 — full siblings couple 3×4, logic. 5 & 7 share 0 — parents come entirely different founders, genetically unrelated pedigree. block-diagonal pattern typical study multiple independent families. real cohort pedigree often complex (multi-generation, distant relatives), interpretation : larger -diagonal values mean shared ancestry.

title: Getting started with R-itable
text: simulate small multi-family cohort — 80 nuclear families, 2 parents + 3 offspring — three phenotypes different true h² values. mirrors real pedigree phenotype CSV files.
code: library(Ritable)  # ---- 1. Simulate pedigree --------------------------------------------------- set.seed(2026) n_fam <- 80  ped <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(n_fam), function(f) {   base <- (f - 1L) * 5L   data.frame(     id  = base + 1:5,     pat = c(0L, 0L, base + 1L, base + 1L, base + 1L),     mom = c(0L, 0L, base + 2L, base + 2L, base + 2L),     sex = c(1L, 2L, sample(1:2, 3, replace = TRUE))   ) }))  # ---- 2. Simulate phenotypes for offspring ----------------------------------- # Three traits with approximate h2: bmi ~0.6, sbp ~0.35, hdl ~0.5 simulate_trait <- function(ped, n_fam, h2, seed) {   set.seed(seed)   genetic  <- rep(rnorm(n_fam, 0, sqrt(h2)),       each = 5)   residual <- rnorm(nrow(ped),          0, sqrt(1 - h2))   genetic + residual }  pheno_all <- data.frame(   bmi = simulate_trait(ped, n_fam, h2 = 0.60, seed = 1),   sbp = simulate_trait(ped, n_fam, h2 = 0.35, seed = 2),   hdl = simulate_trait(ped, n_fam, h2 = 0.50, seed = 3) )  off_rows <- ped$pat != 0L dat <- data.frame(   IID     = ped$id[off_rows],   age     = round(runif(sum(off_rows), 20, 75)),   sex_num = ped$sex[off_rows],   bmi     = pheno_all$bmi[off_rows],   sbp     = pheno_all$sbp[off_rows],   hdl     = pheno_all$hdl[off_rows] ) dat$age2 <- dat$age^2  # ---- 3. Build GRM once — reuse for all models ------------------------------- A <- build_grm(ped, study_ids = dat$IID)  # ---- 4. Define covariate models --------------------------------------------- covs_list <- list(   unadj = NULL,   cov1  = c("age", "sex_num"),   cov2  = c("age", "sex_num", "age2") )  # ---- 5. Batch estimation ---------------------------------------------------- res <- herit_batch(   traits    = c("bmi", "sbp", "hdl"),   grm       = A,   data      = dat,   covs_list = covs_list )  res #>       label trait       covariates   n     h2     se  ci_lo ci_hi pval #> 1 bmi_unadj   bmi                  240 0.9990 0.1296 0.8376     1    0 #> 2 sbp_unadj   sbp                  240 0.8054 0.1392 0.5302     1    0 #> 3 hdl_unadj   hdl                  240 0.8010 0.1394 0.5256     1    0 #> 4  bmi_cov1   bmi      age+sex_num 240 0.9990 0.1313 0.8303     1    0 #> 5  sbp_cov1   sbp      age+sex_num 240 0.8015 0.1402 0.5244     1    0 #> 6  hdl_cov1   hdl      age+sex_num 240 0.8026 0.1395 0.5269     1    0 #> 7  bmi_cov2   bmi age+sex_num+age2 240 0.9990 0.1317 0.8251     1    0 #> 8  sbp_cov2   sbp age+sex_num+age2 240 0.8004 0.1401 0.5233     1    0 #> 9  hdl_cov2   hdl age+sex_num+age2 240 0.8052 0.1405 0.5271     1    0 #>   var_covariates sigma2_a sigma2_e #> 1             NA  0.90510  0.00091 #> 2             NA  0.77409  0.18708 #> 3             NA  0.76987  0.19130 #> 4         0.0209  0.89834  0.00090 #> 5         0.0087  0.76543  0.18952 #> 6         0.0070  0.76629  0.18849 #> 7         0.0307  0.89482  0.00090 #> 8         0.0121  0.76155  0.18992 #> 9         0.0094  0.76945  0.18617 if (requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)) {   plot_forest(res, model_filter = "cov2",               title = "Heritability estimates (age + sex + age\u00b2)") }

title: Twin cohorts: MZ relatedness, household effects, and bivariate correlations
text: Getting started vignette covers herit_vc() herit_batch(): single-component (additive genetic, -) heritability general family pedigrees. Twin studies add three things vignette doesn’t cover: Monozygotic (MZ) twins genetically identical (relatedness 1.0, ordinary full-sibling 0.5) – build_grm()’s mz_col argument. Twins reared together share genes – common/shared environment (“household”, C classic ACE model) can confounded additive genetic () effects unless explicitly test – build_household() herit_ace(). Twin designs classical setting asking whether two traits share genetic environmental causes – bivariate genetic/environmental correlation, via herit_bivar() herit_bivar_batch(). vignette builds small synthetic twin cohort walks three.

title: Twin cohorts: MZ relatedness, household effects, and bivariate correlations
text: twin pedigree looks like pedigree, two extra columns build_grm() build_household() care : MZ-twin label (shared monozygotic pairs) household ID (shared anyone reared together, MZ DZ). ’ll simulate 30 MZ pairs 30 DZ pairs (120 individuals total), pair synthetic founder “parents” (build_grm() needs founders present rows, even – – aren’t real study participants). Two correlated phenotypes simulated known genetic environmental correlations, known answer check herit_bivar() later.
code: # Tiny base-R replacement for MASS::mvrnorm for a 2x2 covariance -- R-itable # has no dependency on MASS, so the vignette doesn't introduce one either. rbinorm <- function(n, rho) {   z <- matrix(rnorm(2 * n), n, 2)   L <- chol(matrix(c(1, rho, rho, 1), 2, 2))   z %*% L }  set.seed(2026) n_mz <- 30 n_dz <- 30 n_pairs <- n_mz + n_dz  rhoG_true <- 0.85  # true genetic correlation (before dilution from DZ noise) rhoE_true <- 0.35  # true environmental correlation  ped_rows   <- vector("list", n_pairs) pheno_rows <- vector("list", n_pairs)  # Family-level genetic latents for the two traits, correlated at rhoG_true fam_g <- rbinorm(n_pairs, rhoG_true)  for (i in seq_len(n_pairs)) {   is_mz  <- i <= n_mz   fa     <- paste0("F", i)   mo     <- paste0("M", i)   id1    <- (i - 1L) * 2L + 1L   id2    <- id1 + 1L   mztwin <- if (is_mz) paste0("MZ", i) else NA_character_   hh     <- paste0("HH", i)   pair_sex <- if (is_mz) rep(sample(1:2, 1), 2) else sample(1:2, 2, replace = TRUE)    ped_rows[[i]] <- data.frame(     id = c(id1, id2), pat = c(fa, fa), mom = c(mo, mo),     mztwin = c(mztwin, mztwin), zygosity = if (is_mz) "MZ" else "DZ",     sex = pair_sex, hhid = c(hh, hh), stringsAsFactors = FALSE   )    # Additive genetic effect: shared fully within MZ pairs; shared "family"   # component plus individual-specific noise within DZ pairs (average   # relatedness 0.5).   g1_fam <- fam_g[i, 1]; g2_fam <- fam_g[i, 2]   if (is_mz) {     g1 <- c(g1_fam, g1_fam)     g2 <- c(g2_fam, g2_fam)   } else {     g1 <- g1_fam + rnorm(2)     g2 <- g2_fam + rnorm(2)   }    # Environmental effect, correlated at rhoE_true, independent across twins   env <- rbinorm(2, rhoE_true)    y1 <- sqrt(0.5) * g1 + sqrt(0.5) * env[, 1]   y2 <- sqrt(0.4) * g2 + sqrt(0.6) * env[, 2]    pheno_rows[[i]] <- data.frame(id = c(id1, id2), sleep_quality = y1, anxiety = y2) }  ped_df   <- do.call(rbind, ped_rows) pheno_df <- do.call(rbind, pheno_rows)  # build_grm() needs founders present as their own rows (pat/mom = NA) fathers  <- unique(ped_df$pat) mothers  <- unique(ped_df$mom) founders <- data.frame(   id = c(fathers, mothers), pat = NA, mom = NA, mztwin = NA, zygosity = NA,   sex = c(rep(1, length(fathers)), rep(2, length(mothers))), hhid = NA,   stringsAsFactors = FALSE ) full_ped <- rbind(founders, ped_df)  head(ped_df) #>   id pat mom mztwin zygosity sex hhid #> 1  1  F1  M1    MZ1       MZ   1  HH1 #> 2  2  F1  M1    MZ1       MZ   1  HH1 #> 3  3  F2  M2    MZ2       MZ   2  HH2 #> 4  4  F2  M2    MZ2       MZ   2  HH2 #> 5  5  F3  M3    MZ3       MZ   1  HH3 #> 6  6  F3  M3    MZ3       MZ   1  HH3

what: 2. Build the GRM with MZ relatedness
title: Twin cohorts: MZ relatedness, household effects, and bivariate correlations
text: Without mz_col, build_grm() treats every pair ordinary full siblings (relatedness 0.5) – correct DZ twins, wrong MZ twins. Pass mz_col fix : MZ pair’s -diagonal 1.0; DZ pair’s ordinary full-sibling 0.5. mz_col also handles larger groups (e.g. MZ triplets) – every pairwise combination within labelled group marked, just first two. build_household() builds companion matrix shared-environment (“household”) effect, hhid grouping column:
code: A <- build_grm(full_ped, study_ids = ped_df$id, mz_col = "mztwin")  mz_ids <- ped_df$id[ped_df$zygosity == "MZ"][1:2] dz_ids <- ped_df$id[ped_df$zygosity == "DZ"][1:2]  A[as.character(mz_ids), as.character(mz_ids)] #>   1 2 #> 1 1 1 #> 2 1 1 A[as.character(dz_ids), as.character(dz_ids)] #>     61  62 #> 61 1.0 0.5 #> 62 0.5 1.0 C <- build_household(ped_df$hhid, ped_df$id) C[as.character(mz_ids), as.character(mz_ids)] #>   1 2 #> 1 1 1 #> 2 1 1

title: Twin cohorts: MZ relatedness, household effects, and bivariate correlations
text: classical twin design lets decompose phenotypic variance Additive genetic, Common/shared environment, unique Environment components – data actually support telling C apart. herit_ace() fits four nested models (sporadic, AE-, CE-, full ACE) gives two comparisons matter: Reading output: p_c_vs_sporadic – familial (shared) effect , ignoring moment whether ’s genetic environmental? small p-value means yes. p_ace_vs_ae – additive genetic effects model, adding separate household term improve fit? (large p-value, /c2_ace near 0), C separately identifiable sample – household signal detected gets fully absorbed genetic term estimated jointly. common, real finding twin studies modest samples, bug: report simpler AE model case (h2_ae), note limitation.
code: dat <- pheno_df dat$IID <- dat$id  res_ace <- herit_ace("sleep_quality", grm = A, household = C, data = dat, id_col = "IID") #> ✔ sleep_quality  n=120  h2(AE)=0.565  c2(CE)=0.22  c2(ACE)=0  p(ACE vs AE)=0.5 str(res_ace) #> List of 14 #>  $ trait              : chr "sleep_quality" #>  $ n                  : int 120 #>  $ loglik_sporadic    : num -55.8 #>  $ loglik_ae          : num -51.3 #>  $ loglik_ce          : num -54.3 #>  $ loglik_ace         : num -51.3 #>  $ h2_ae              : num 0.565 #>  $ c2_ce              : num 0.22 #>  $ h2_ace             : num 0.565 #>  $ c2_ace             : num 0 #>  $ chisq_c_vs_sporadic: num 2.97 #>  $ p_c_vs_sporadic    : num 0.0423 #>  $ chisq_ace_vs_ae    : num 0 #>  $ p_ace_vs_ae        : num 0.5

title: Twin cohorts: MZ relatedness, household effects, and bivariate correlations
text: herit_ace() can adjust covariates via covs, optional automatic screening replicates SOLAR Eclipse’s polygenic -screen algorithm (confirmed SOLAR’s source, assumed): fit AE model candidate covariates, likelihood-ratio-test one individually full model, drop p >= prob_level (default 0.10, SOLAR’s default). final covariate set used four nested models, keeping sporadic/AE/CE/ACE comparisons validly nested. Pass screen = FALSE include every covariate covs unconditionally, skipping LRT screening step entirely.
code: # A synthetic covariate that genuinely predicts sleep_quality, and one # that's pure noise -- screening should keep the first and drop the second # (though with any single random draw, a pure-noise covariate can # occasionally clear a p < 0.10 threshold by chance, same as any # significance test). set.seed(1) dat$age       <- round(runif(nrow(dat), 20, 60)) dat$predictor <- dat$sleep_quality * 2 + rnorm(nrow(dat), sd = 0.1)  res_ace_cov <- herit_ace("sleep_quality", grm = A, household = C, data = dat,                          covs = c("age", "predictor"), id_col = "IID") #> ℹ sleep_quality: covariate screening kept 1/2 (predictor) #> ✔ sleep_quality  n=120  h2(AE)=0.028  c2(CE)=0  c2(ACE)=0  p(ACE vs AE)=0.5 res_ace_cov$covariate_lrt_p  # each candidate's individual LRT p-value #>           age     predictor  #>  9.029771e-01 7.963235e-131 res_ace_cov$covs_kept        # the ones that survived screening #> [1] "predictor"

title: Twin cohorts: MZ relatedness, household effects, and bivariate correlations
text: herit_bivar() asks different question: two traits, much phenotypic correlation explained shared genetic causes (rhoG) vs shared environmental causes (rhoE)? simulated rhoG_true = 0.85 (diluted somewhat individual-specific genetic noise added DZ pairs) rhoE_true = 0.35; herit_bivar() recovers clearly significant genetic correlation smaller, non-significant environmental one – realistic pattern (trait pair looks correlated mainly genetic, environmental, reasons). rhoP derived phenotypic correlation implied rhoG, rhoE, two univariate heritabilities:
code: res_biv <- herit_bivar("sleep_quality", "anxiety", grm = A, data = dat, id_col = "IID") #> ✔ sleep_quality x anxiety  n=120  rhoG=0.675 (p=0.0081)  rhoE=0.24 (p=0.201) str(res_biv) #> List of 12 #>  $ trait1    : chr "sleep_quality" #>  $ trait2    : chr "anxiety" #>  $ n         : int 120 #>  $ n_complete: int 120 #>  $ h2_1      : num 0.465 #>  $ h2_2      : num 0.523 #>  $ rhoG      : num 0.675 #>  $ rhoE      : num 0.24 #>  $ rhoP      : num 0.454 #>  $ p_rhoG    : num 0.0081 #>  $ p_rhoE    : num 0.201 #>  $ p_rhoP    : num 6.69e-06 with(res_biv, rhoG * sqrt(h2_1 * h2_2) + rhoE * sqrt((1 - h2_1) * (1 - h2_2))) #> [1] 0.4542334 res_biv$rhoP #> [1] 0.4542

what: 5. Many trait pairs at once: herit_bivar_batch()
title: Twin cohorts: MZ relatedness, household effects, and bivariate correlations
text: Real analyses usually involve one trait interest panel others. herit_bivar_batch() iterates herit_bivar() set pairs applies Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction separately within three p-value families (rhoG, rhoE, rhoP) – matching convention used cross-checking SOLAR Eclipse output (see ?herit_bivar_batch). returned data frame one row per pair, q_rhoG, q_rhoE, q_rhoP alongside raw p-values.
code: # Illustrative only -- 'anxiety' is the only second trait in this vignette's # toy dataset; in a real analysis this would be a panel of phenotypes. pairs <- data.frame(   trait1 = "sleep_quality",   trait2 = "anxiety" )  herit_bivar_batch(pairs, grm = A, data = dat, id_col = "IID")

title: Twin cohorts: MZ relatedness, household effects, and bivariate correlations
text: herit_ace() herit_bivar() use direct numerical maximum likelihood (Cholesky-based GLS) rather herit_vc()’s eigendecomposition shortcut, since household term second trait’s cross-covariance don’t general share eigenvectors additive genetic matrix. validated real SOLAR Eclipse output twin dataset documented ground-truth comparison – see NEWS.md numbers methodology, ?herit_bivar “validated” means precisely (bit-identical SOLAR, since ’s achievable independent numerical optimisers, matching several decimal places large majority trait pairs checked).

title: R-itable — Pedigree-based heritability estimation
text: R-itable (library(Ritable)) estimates narrow-sense heritability (h²) quantitative traits pedigree-based family cohort studies. implements profile-likelihood variance-components approach equivalent SOLAR Eclipse — without proprietary dependencies, compiled code, external binaries. Built neuroimaging biomedical cohorts need run heritability dozens traits across multiple covariate models get results can trace back first principles.

title: R-itable — Pedigree-based heritability estimation
text: 🔬 Profile-likelihood VC estimator — eigendecomposition GRM, 1-D optimisation, exact LRT one-sided χ²(1) boundary correction (matching SOLAR). 👯 Twin cohorts — build_grm(mz_col = ...) gives monozygotic pairs (larger groups) correct kinship 1.0, instead ordinary full-sibling 0.5. 🏠 Household/common-environment effects — herit_ace() fits nested sporadic/AE/CE/ACE models tests whether C jointly identifiable sample, optional SOLAR--screen-style automatic covariate screening (covs = ...). 🔗 Bivariate genetic/environmental correlations — herit_bivar() / herit_bivar_batch() estimate rhoG, rhoE, derived rhoP trait pairs, LRTs Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction across batch. 📐 Profile-likelihood CIs — Wald ±1.96 SE; proper asymmetric intervals via uniroot(). 🔄 INT transformation — inverse-normal transform applied internally; also exported int_transform() use pipelines. 📦 Batch mode — herit_batch() iterates traits × covariate models returns tidy data frame, ready tables figures. 🌲 Forest plots — plot_forest() immediate visualisation batch output (requires ggplot2). 🧩 Minimal dependencies — core functions require base R, kinship2, rlang, cli.

code: # GRM with MZ-twin relatedness override (mztwin_col groups MZ pairs/triplets) A <- build_grm(twin_pedigree, study_ids = twin_data$IID, mz_col = "mztwin") C <- build_household(twin_pedigree$hhid, twin_pedigree$id)  # A vs C identifiability: sporadic / AE / CE / full ACE herit_ace("anxiety_score", grm = A, household = C, data = twin_data, id_col = "IID")  # ...with automatic covariate screening (SOLAR's polygenic -screen algorithm: # single-pass LRT test of each candidate, drop if p >= prob_level) twin_data$age_sex <- twin_data$age * twin_data$sex res <- herit_ace("anxiety_score", grm = A, household = C, data = twin_data,                 covs = c("age", "sex", "age_sex"), id_col = "IID") res$covs_kept      # covariates that survived screening res$covariate_lrt_p # each candidate's individual LRT p-value  # Bivariate genetic/environmental correlation between two traits herit_bivar("anxiety_score", "depression_score", grm = A, data = twin_data, id_col = "IID")  # Many trait pairs at once, with BH-FDR correction per correlation type pairs <- data.frame(   trait1 = c("anxiety_score", "depression_score"),   trait2 = c("sleep_quality", "sleep_quality") ) herit_bivar_batch(pairs, grm = A, data = twin_data, id_col = "IID")

what: Ritable: Pedigree-Based Heritability Estimation for Family Cohort Studies — Ritable-package
title: Ritable: Pedigree-Based Heritability Estimation for Family Cohort Studies — Ritable-package
text: Provides profile-likelihood general maximum-likelihood variance-components estimation narrow-sense heritability (h2), household/common-environment effects (c2), bivariate genetic environmental correlations quantitative traits family cohort twin studies. Additive genetic relationship matrices built pedigrees via 'kinship2', including monozygotic-twin relatedness overrides. Phenotypes inverse-normal transformed internally. Likelihood-ratio tests use one-sided chi-squared boundary correction equivalent SOLAR Eclipse. Ninety-five percent confidence intervals derived profile likelihood rather Wald approximations. Batch estimation many traits trait pairs returns tidy data frames ready downstream visualisation (forest plots, heatmaps) includes Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction bivariate correlation batches.

title: Build an additive genetic relationship matrix from a pedigree — build_grm
text: ped_df data frame least columns id, pat, mom, sex. Missing parents NA 0. sex numeric: 1 = male, 2 = female (value recoded 1 warning). study_ids Character integer vector IDs study subjects whose sub-matrix extracted. Defaults IDs ped_df. id_col, pat_col, mom_col, sex_col Column names four required pedigree fields. Defaults "id", "pat", "mom", "sex". mz_col Optional column name ped_df identifying monozygotic twin/multiple groups (e.g. shared family label present MZ sets, blank/NA everyone else, MZTWIN column). pairwise combinations individuals sharing non-blank, non-NA value mz_col passed kinship2::pedigree() monozygotic (code = 1), overriding default full-sibling kinship 0.25 correct MZ kinship 0.5 (= 1.0). Groups size \(\geq\) 3 (e.g. MZ triplets) supported: every pair within group marked. NULL (default) disables reproduces prior behaviour exactly.

title: Build an additive genetic relationship matrix from a pedigree — build_grm
text: symmetric numeric matrix dimension length(study_ids) x length(study_ids), diagonal entries equal 1 non-inbred individuals row/column names matching study_ids.

title: Build an additive genetic relationship matrix from a pedigree — build_grm
text: function calls kinship2::kinship() full pedigree (including founders), multiplies 2 obtain additive relationship matrix, finally subsets study_ids. Including founders pedigree ensures kinship coefficients study subjects connected founders estimated correctly. twin cohorts, pat/mom typically synthetic per-pair founder labels rather genotyped individuals; founders still present rows ped_df (pat/mom set NA) kinship2::pedigree() can resolve family structure. Without mz_col, twins treated ordinary full siblings (= 0.5); supplying mz_col corrects MZ pairs = 1.0 leaving DZ pairs (already correct full-sibling kinship) unchanged.

title: Build an additive genetic relationship matrix from a pedigree — build_grm
code: # Minimal two-generation pedigree: two couples, four offspring ped <- data.frame(   id  = 1:8,   pat = c(0, 0, 0, 0, 1, 1, 3, 3),   mom = c(0, 0, 0, 0, 2, 2, 4, 4),   sex = c(1, 2, 1, 2, 1, 2, 1, 2) ) A <- build_grm(ped, study_ids = 5:8) round(A, 3) #>     5   6   7   8 #> 5 1.0 0.5 0.0 0.0 #> 6 0.5 1.0 0.0 0.0 #> 7 0.0 0.0 1.0 0.5 #> 8 0.0 0.0 0.5 1.0  # With an MZ-twin column: subjects 7 and 8 are MZ (forced to the same sex, # since kinship2 requires MZ pairs to share sex -- ordinarily they would # already match) ped$sex[ped$id %in% c(7, 8)] <- 1 ped$mztwin <- c(NA, NA, NA, NA, NA, NA, "MZ1", "MZ1") A_mz <- build_grm(ped, study_ids = 5:8, mz_col = "mztwin") round(A_mz, 3)  # A[7,8] = 1.0 instead of 0.5 #>     5   6 7 8 #> 5 1.0 0.5 0 0 #> 6 0.5 1.0 0 0 #> 7 0.0 0.0 1 1 #> 8 0.0 0.0 1 1

what: A vs C identifiability check (ACE model comparison) — herit_ace
title: A vs C identifiability check (ACE model comparison) — herit_ace
text: Fits four nested variance-component models single quantitative trait – sporadic (familial effect), polygenic/AE (additive genetic ), household/CE (common environment ), full ACE (C estimated jointly) – returns log-likelihoods together two likelihood-ratio tests needed judge whether C separately identifiable sample: CE vs sporadic (familial signal ?) ACE vs AE (C add anything model?). mirrors SOLAR Eclipse's house / polygenic -screen model-comparison workflow (see solar_full_analysis.tcl, Part 3).

title: A vs C identifiability check (ACE model comparison) — herit_ace
code: herit_ace(   trait,   grm,   household,   data,   covs = NULL,   screen = TRUE,   prob_level = 0.1,   id_col = "IID",   transform = TRUE,   min_n = 80L,   verbose = TRUE )

title: A vs C identifiability check (ACE model comparison) — herit_ace
text: trait Character string: name trait column data. grm Numeric matrix: additive genetic relationship matrix, returned build_grm(). household Numeric matrix: household indicator matrix, returned build_household(). Must row/column names grm. data Data frame containing id_col, trait, covs. covs Optional character vector covariate column names data (e.g. c("age", "sex", "age_sex", "age2", "age2_sex") SOLAR's standard age/sex/agesex/age^2/age^2sex set – construct interaction polynomial terms ordinary columns calling, convention herit_vc()). Covariates standardised internally. Default NULL (covariates, matching prior behaviour exactly). screen Logical. covs given, apply SOLAR-style automatic covariate screening (see Details) rather including covs unconditionally. Default TRUE. Ignored covs NULL. prob_level Screening significance threshold. Default 0.10, matching SOLAR Eclipse's default (confirmed source, lib/solar.tcl proc polygenic: set probability_level 0.1). id_col Name individual ID column data. Default "IID". transform Logical. Apply int_transform() trait fitting. Default TRUE, matching SOLAR Eclipse convention skewed phenotypes. min_n Minimum number complete observations required. Default 80L. verbose Logical. Print progress via cli. Default TRUE.

title: A vs C identifiability check (ACE model comparison) — herit_ace
text: named list elements: trait Trait name. n Sample size dropping missing values. loglik_sporadic, loglik_ae, loglik_ce, loglik_ace Log-likelihoods four nested models (fit final covariate set – see Details). h2_ae Heritability AE model. c2_ce Common-environment proportion CE model. h2_ace, c2_ace Joint estimates full ACE model. chisq_c_vs_sporadic, p_c_vs_sporadic One-sided boundary LRT CE vs sporadic (evidence familial effect ). chisq_ace_vs_ae, p_ace_vs_ae One-sided boundary LRT ACE vs AE (evidence C adds anything estimated). near-zero statistic c2_ace near 0 boundary indicates C jointly identifiable sample – report simpler AE model (see package vignette / Leocadio-Miguel et al. companion analyses). covs_tested, covs_kept, covs_dropped Present covs supplied screen = TRUE: full candidate list, ones retained (p < prob_level), ones dropped. covariate_lrt_p Present covs supplied screen = TRUE: named numeric vector candidate covariate's individual LRT p-value full-covariate AE model. Returns NULL n < min_n.

title: A vs C identifiability check (ACE model comparison) — herit_ace
text: Unlike herit_vc(), diagonalises single variance component via eigen(), function estimates one two variance components jointly direct numerical maximum likelihood full n x n covariance matrix (Cholesky-based GLS), since household indicator C general share eigenvectors. Model: Omega = sigma2_p * [h2*+ c2*C + (1 - h2 - c2)*], jointly estimated ACE model via multi-start Nelder-Mead logit-reparametrised (h2, c2) (guaranteeing h2, c2 >= 0 h2 + c2 < 1); AE CE 1-D special cases. Covariates () enter mean structure: E[y] = X %*% beta, X including intercept plus (standardised) columns named covs. Covariate screening (covs given screen = TRUE): matches SOLAR Eclipse's polygenic -screen, confirmed source (lib/solar.tcl proc polygenic) rather assumed. SOLAR's algorithm single pass, iterative backward elimination: fit AE model candidate covariates, covariate individually, fit AE model just one covariate removed compute likelihood-ratio test full-covariate model (chi-squared(1), boundary-corrected, since covariate coefficient boundary parameter). covariate p >= prob_level dropped; remaining covariates kept. happens , AE model specifically (separately CE/ACE) – SOLAR's script can principle screen separately per model context, using one shared covariate set four nested models keeps sporadic/AE/CE/ACE comparisons validly nested (valid LRT requires compared models share mean structure). LRTs h2/c2: one-sided chi-squared(1) boundary correction, herit_vc(), since null hypotheses (c2 = 0, h2 = 0) sit boundary parameter space.

what: Bivariate genetic and environmental correlation between two traits — herit_bivar
title: Bivariate genetic and environmental correlation between two traits — herit_bivar
text: Fits bivariate AE variance-components model two quantitative traits estimates additive-genetic correlation (rhoG), non-shared environmental correlation (rhoE), derived phenotypic correlation (rhoP = rhoGsqrt(h2_1h2_2) + rhoEsqrt((1-h2_1)(1-h2_2))), together likelihood-ratio tests rhoG = 0, rhoE = 0, joint test rhoP = 0 (rhoG = rhoE = 0). mirrors SOLAR Eclipse's polygenic -testrhog / -testrhoe bivariate output (see solar_full_analysis.tcl, Part 5).

title: Bivariate genetic and environmental correlation between two traits — herit_bivar
text: trait1, trait2 Character strings: names two trait columns data. grm Numeric matrix: additive genetic relationship matrix, returned build_grm(). data Data frame containing id_col, trait1, trait2. id_col Name individual ID column data. Default "IID". transform Logical. Apply int_transform() traits fitting. Default TRUE. min_n Minimum number individuals contributing analysis sample required (individual counts least one trait1, trait2 observed – see Details). Default 80L. verbose Logical. Print progress via cli. Default TRUE.

title: Bivariate genetic and environmental correlation between two traits — herit_bivar
text: named list elements: trait1, trait2 Trait names. n Number individuals contributing analysis (union trait1 /trait2 observed – see Details). n_complete Number individuals traits observed. Equal n neither trait missing data. h2_1, h2_2 Heritability trait joint bivariate model. rhoG, rhoE, rhoP Genetic, environmental, derived phenotypic correlations. p_rhoG, p_rhoE LRT p-values rhoG = 0 rhoE = 0 (standard two-sided chi-squared(1); correlations boundary parameters). p_rhoP LRT p-value joint null rhoG = rhoE = 0 (chi-squared(2)). Returns NULL n < min_n.

title: Bivariate genetic and environmental correlation between two traits — herit_bivar
text: Model: traits stacked 2n-vector block covariance Sigma = [[sigma2_g1*+ sigma2_e1*, rhoG*sqrt(sigma2_g1*sigma2_g2)*+ rhoE*sqrt(sigma2_e1*sigma2_e2)*], [..., sigma2_g2*+ sigma2_e2*]], sigma2_g_i = h2_i * sigma2_p_i sigma2_e_i = (1-h2_i) * sigma2_p_i. six free parameters (h2_1, h2_2, rhoG, rhoE, sigma2_p1, sigma2_p2) estimated jointly multi-start Nelder-Mead ML reparametrised scale (logit h2, atanh correlations, log variances) constraints hold automatically. Missing data: either trait missing values, individuals missing exactly one two traits still included analysis sample, contributing observed trait's marginal likelihood, matching SOLAR Eclipse's default UnbalancedTraits behaviour (individuals excluded traits, ID, missing). statistically appropriate dropping (information used usual MAR assumption) matches SOLAR exactly combined SOLAR-exact inormal tie handling int_transform() – see NEWS.md validation. neither trait missing data (common case), reduces fast eigenbasis computation – unbalanced path used needed, since exploit eigenbasis shortcut (missingness pattern individual-specific, joint covariance longer shares common eigenbasis across n individuals). Numerical robustness: traits standardised unit variance fitting. h2 correlations scale-invariant, changes nothing true ML answer, avoids real failure mode raw (non-INT-transformed) traits extreme variance – e.g. data-entry problem producing values billions – unstandardised covariance matrix loses floating-point precision. rhoG/rhoE also bounded [-0.9, 0.9], matching SOLAR's actual default parameter bounds (confirmed source, just documentation – see NEWS.md) rather mathematical [-1, 1]. herit_ace(), unbalanced path uses direct numerical ML full covariance matrix rather eigendecomposition shortcut. Validated Gomes et al. twin dataset (31 trait pairs), combining correct per-trait inverse-normal transform selection, SOLAR-exact inormal tie handling (see int_transform()), unbalanced-trait handling, numerical robustness fixes : 28 31 pairs match SOLAR Eclipse 4 decimal places exactly rhoG rhoE, 31 pairs agree nominal significance . 2 remaining pairs involve single phenotype (CRONOTIPO_MCTQ_m validation dataset) produces wildly different results SOLAR's reported values even fully numerically-robust fit – strong evidence underlying data values differ package's copy whatever SOLAR actually run , modelling numerical gap package. See NEWS.md.

title: Profile-likelihood variance-components heritability estimation — herit_vc
text: trait Character string: name trait column data. grm Numeric matrix: additive genetic relationship matrix individuals data, returned build_grm(). Row column names must match ID column data. data Data frame containing id_col, trait, covariate columns. covs Character vector covariate column names, NULL intercept-model. Covariates mean-centred scaled unit variance fitting. id_col Name individual ID column data. Default "IID". label Optional string label model (used batch output). NULL, defaults "<trait>_adj" "<trait>_unadj". min_n Minimum number complete observations required attempt estimation. Models fewer observations return NULL silently. Default 80. ci_level Confidence level profile-likelihood interval. Default 0.95. verbose Logical. Print progress console. Default TRUE.

title: Profile-likelihood variance-components heritability estimation — herit_vc
text: named list elements: label Model label. trait Trait name. covariates Covariate names joined "+", "". n Sample size dropping missing values. h2 MLE narrow-sense heritability. se Standard error profile-likelihood curvature (Wald). ci_lo, ci_hi Profile-likelihood confidence interval bounds. pval One-sided LRT p-value chi-squared(1) boundary correction. var_covariates Proportion phenotypic variance explained fixed-effect covariates (R² INT-transformed phenotype). NA unadjusted models. Corresponds "variance explained" column Leocadio-Miguel et al. (2025). sigma2_a Additive genetic variance (sigma²_g SOLAR notation). sigma2_e Residual environmental variance (sigma²_e). Returns NULL n < min_n GRM subset degenerate.

title: Profile-likelihood variance-components heritability estimation — herit_vc
text: Model: Omega = sigma2_p [h2 + (1 - h2) I_n] Optimisation: eigendecomposition followed 1-D profile-likelihood optimisation h2 (0, 1) using coarse grid seed stats::optimize(). LRT: one-sided chi-squared(1) boundary correction – null boundary parameter space (h2 = 0), p-value halved relative standard chi-squared test. matches SOLAR Eclipse convention. CIs: derived uniroot() profile log-likelihood, falling back Wald interval root-finding fails.

title: Inverse-normal (rank-based) transformation — int_transform
text: Applies rank-based inverse-normal transformation (INT) numeric vector, placing empirical quantiles onto standard normal scale.

title: Inverse-normal (rank-based) transformation — int_transform
code: int_transform(x, method = c("vdw", "blom"), ties = "average")

title: Inverse-normal (rank-based) transformation — int_transform
text: x Numeric vector. NAs preserved. method INT formula use. "vdw" (default) exactly replicates SOLAR Eclipse's inormal command, confirmed SOLAR's actual source (lib/solar.tcl, proc inormal): sort ascending, assign z_i = qnorm(/ (n+1)) individual rank position , tied values average resulting z-scores individual rank positions (z-score averaged rank – differ nonlinear qnorm whenever tied block symmetric around n/2, e.g. large block tied values one tail, zero-inflated phenotypes). "blom" Blom (1958) transformation, qnorm((r-0.5)/n) conventional averaged-rank tie handling, used R-itable prior fix (incorrect) belief matched SOLAR. ties Method passed base::rank() method = "blom". Ignored method = "vdw", always uses SOLAR's tie handling (see Details). Default "average".

title: Inverse-normal (rank-based) transformation — int_transform
text: numeric vector length x, NAs positions non-missing values transformed approximate normality.

title: Inverse-normal (rank-based) transformation — int_transform
text: method = "vdw" ties, Van der Waerden (1952) transformation, qnorm(r_i / (n+1)), bit-identical . ties, tied individuals get mean qnorm(/(n+1)) tied rank positions , exactly matching SOLAR's inormal. distinction matters heavily-tied data; confirmed fully resolve remaining discrepancy R-itable SOLAR Eclipse zero-inflated phenotypes Gomes et al. validation dataset (\(>\) 25% tied values) – see NEWS.md. method = "blom": $$\Phi^{-1}\!\left(\frac{r_i - 0.5}{n}\right)$$ using base::rank()'s ties argument tie handling (default "average", .e. z-score averaged rank – conventional approach formula, SOLAR's).

title: Inverse-normal (rank-based) transformation — int_transform
code: set.seed(1) x <- rexp(200, rate = 0.5)   # right-skewed hist(x,              main = "Raw")  hist(int_transform(x), main = "INT (SOLAR-matching Van der Waerden)")   # Heavy ties (e.g. zero-inflated activity duration): SOLAR's tie handling # (default) differs meaningfully from naive rank-average tie handling. y <- c(rep(0, 40), round(runif(60, 1, 100))) int_transform(y)[1]                        # SOLAR-exact #> [1] -0.9393459 qnorm(rank(y, ties.method = "average")[1] / (length(y) + 1))  # naive #> [1] -0.8310585
